text.content: CWAM B5 VOM R8 high-utilization B128 formal 20k

Test whether the R8 B128 no-checkpointing configuration can complete a stable 20,000-step action-policy run while preserving policy dependence on aligned object-local visual memory and improving effective B200 utilization over R7.

Reach exactly 20,000 finite optimizer steps on 8 B200s without OOM, traceback, NCCL failure, or nonfinite action gradients; write complete 8-rank model/optimizer/scheduler/trainer checkpoints every 1,000 steps including step 20,000; run matched aligned/zero/shuffle validation every 500 steps and retain at least 1% aligned action-loss improvement over both interventions at final validation. Closed-loop policy success is a separate required evaluation and cannot be inferred from training completion or offline loss.

R4 step-500 model-only warm start; fresh optimizer/scheduler/trainer at step 0; R6-A dynamic-exclusive full final-delta architecture; R7 aligned/zero/shuffle intervention-ranking objective weight=1.0, relative margin=1%, warmup=50; 20,000 steps; batch 128/rank, DP8, global 1024; token cap 296000; activation checkpointing none; validation every 500 steps including start; full checkpoint every 1,000 steps.

RoboCasa365 B4 processed split plus 1,143,698-record triple-view Wan latent cache and episode-safe t-36/t-24/t-12 visual-history sidecar; identical stream and online no-future-lookup contract to R7 and the R8 probes.
pyrogpucompute1; 8 x NVIDIA B200 183359 MiB; batch 128/rank; effective global batch 1024; activation checkpointing disabled.

Finite optimizer-step trajectory and action-gradient evidence; seconds/step and samples/s; GPU utilization, memory, and power; aligned/zero/shuffle action loss and relative gains every 500 steps; complete checkpoint inventory every 1,000 steps; subsequent closed-loop task success recorded separately.

B128 was preregistered as the throughput-first selection because the B192 probe increased peak memory to 85.08% but improved mean samples/s by only 0.511%; at a fixed 20,000 optimizer steps B192 would extend runtime from about 34.8 to 51.9 hours. This run therefore uses B128 to maximize optimizer progress per wall-clock hour while retaining the matched aligned-memory intervention gate.
